summary: One intentional governed INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION phase (alias N16-5-F-5-B1-IV, canonical phase 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.30R.5R.2.1R.1R.2R.1R.1R.1R.1.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R.1R). CPIPC: candidate = predecessor N16-5-F-5-B1-IMPL plus exactly one direct .1R segment, independently confirmed via pcae.core.phase_id (same series 149, same branch O, strict ordering greater, candidate.subphase is predecessor.subphase plus one trailing (1,'R') token, unique, no active conflicting phase). I_ENTRY (predecessor implementation phase-entry SHA) = a6455ef1ef130d77c01aa3b2a2d7833f5eb8cb5e, independently re-derived from git log, not adopted from the predecessor's own prose. Independently reconstructed the F-5-B1 implementation from primary source rather than adopting the predecessor's report: git diff --stat confirms exactly the 2 claimed production files changed (hpac_protected_admin_writer.py, hpac_certification_coordinator.py), pure additions; scripts/hpac_certification_admin.py and pyproject.toml confirmed untouched; contract/schema diff since I_ENTRY confirmed empty (HPAC-PAWA-001 v1.4 byte-unchanged). MATERIAL FINDING: consumer authenticity for recognized_certification_read_authority is spoofable. The shared _detect_caller_module(explicit) helper (pre-existing since before I_ENTRY, shared verbatim with production_writer/certification_writer) returns any caller-supplied _caller_module value verbatim with no runtime gate, before ever consulting the real call stack. A fresh IV test suite authored this phase demonstrates, live, that a genuinely unauthorized module (confirmed denied under real stack-based detection with no override) obtains a fully working CertificationReadAuthority handle by passing _caller_module='pcae.core.hpac_certification_coordinator' as an ordinary public keyword argument -- no reflection, no private-attribute access, no monkeypatching. Independently confirmed the predecessor's own 'authorized consumer accepted' positive tests exercise the factory exclusively via this same caller-supplied override from the test module, not via a genuine trusted-caller-identity binding -- i.e. the predecessor's own consumer-authenticity evidence rests on the same seam this IV finds spoofable. The only existing control is a static, source-scanning guard test asserting no non-test module in this checkout happens to pass the argument -- not a runtime authorization boundary, and not effective against any caller outside that repo-local scan. Per HPAC-PAWA-001 v1.4 section 33B/38B and this IV's governing mandatory consumer-authenticity criterion, this is a BLOCKING defect. The pattern pre-dates F-5-B1 (confirmed via git log -S_caller_module) -- F-5-B1 did not introduce it, but its own repair reused it unaddressed, which does not change the verdict for F-5-B1's own read-authority path. No repair was attempted in this verification-only phase; no src/pcae, scripts, or contract-text file was modified. All other independently-checked material properties held: bind ordering (configured-agent bind before protected reads) confirmed by direct control-flow reading; no HPACWriterCapability or writer()/production_writer/certification_writer reachability from the read handle; reads return plain records, never an HPACResolvedRecord carrying authority_seal; the handle is non-serializable (__reduce__ raises TypeError) and cannot be constructed without the existing _PRODUCTION_WRITER_FACTORY_SEAL trust root; the sole approval_presentation guard widening is narrow (one tuple, no wildcard) and no test was deleted/renamed/skipped/inverted in the implementation diff; the predecessor's 72-test suite was re-run fresh and still fully passes (72 passed, 0 failed). A fresh 13-test IV suite (tests/test_phase_..._1r_1r_2r_1r_1r_1r_1_..._n16_5_f5b1_iv.py) captures all of the above as committed, reproducible evidence -- 13 passed, 0 failed (the spoof test passes because it documents the current, insecure behavior, not because the property holds). Full whole-repository fast_green A/B re-attribution and clean-install packaging re-verification were not repeated this phase (disclosed, not concealed) since the confirmed material BLOCK already makes further certification-track matrix completion moot pending repair. VERDICT: F-5-B1: NOT VERIFIED / BLOCKED. F-5: CERTIFICATION BLOCKED PENDING F-5-B2 (consumer-authenticity repair). N-16-5: NOT CLOSED. N-16-6 / N-16-7: OPEN / UNTOUCHED; N-16-7 strictly last. REPORTING-UX-1 still open (non-blocking). Required successor derived but NOT begun: a narrowly-scoped repair phase (alias N16-5-F-5-B2) to bind consumer identity to a non-bypassable trusted mechanism for recognized_certification_read_authority (and, given the shared helper, likely production_writer/certification_writer too).
